1. Lifespan
Mortification
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā uruvelāyaṁ viharati najjā nerañjarāya tīre ajapālanigrodhamūle paṭhamābhisambuddho.
segs.e: At one time, when he was first awakened, the Buddha was staying in Uruvelā at the root of the goatherd’s banyan tree on the bank of the Nerañjarā River.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavato rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṁ cetaso parivitakko udapādi:
segs.e: Then as he was in private retreat this thought came to his mind,
“I am truly freed from that grueling work!

segs.p: Sādhu mutto vatamhi tāya anatthasaṁhitāya dukkarakārikāya.
segs.e: Thank goodness I’m freed from that pointless grueling work.
Thank goodness I’m freed and have attained awakening.”

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā bhagavato cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: And then Māra the Wicked, knowing the Buddha’s train of thought, went up to him and addressed him in verse:
“You’ve left the practice of mortification
by which sons of men purify themselves.
You’re impure, but think yourself pure;
you’ve strayed from the path of purity.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā “māro ayaṁ pāpimā” iti viditvā māraṁ pāpimantaṁ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha, knowing that this was Māra the Wicked, replied to him in verse:
“I realized that it’s pointless;
all that endless mortification
is as futile
as oars and rudder on dry land.
Ethics, immersion, and wisdom:
by developing this path to awakening
I attained ultimate purity.
You’re beaten, terminator!”

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṁ bhagavā, jānāti maṁ sugato”ti, dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.
segs.e: Then Māra the Wicked, thinking, “The Buddha knows me! The Holy One knows me!” miserable and sad, vanished right there.

1. Lifespan
Māra’s Snares (1st)
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā bārāṇasiyaṁ viharati isipatane migadāye.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Varanasi in the deer park at Isipatana.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,
“Mendicants!”
“Venerable sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Mayhaṁ kho, bhikkhave, yoniso manasikārā yoniso sammappadhānā anuttarā vimutti anuppattā, anuttarā vimutti sacchikatā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I have attained and realized supreme freedom through rational application of mind and rational right effort.

segs.p: Tumhepi, bhikkhave, yoniso manasikārā yoniso sammappadhānā anuttaraṁ vimuttiṁ anupāpuṇātha, anuttaraṁ vimuttiṁ sacchikarothā”ti.
segs.e: You too should attain and realize supreme freedom through rational application of mind and rational right effort.”

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then Māra the Wicked went up to the Buddha and addressed him in verse:
“You’re bound by Māra’s snares,
both human and heavenly.
You’re bound by Māra’s bonds:
you won’t escape me, ascetic!”
“I’m freed from Māra’s snares,
both human and heavenly.
I’m freed from Māra’s bonds.
You’re beaten, terminator!”
Then Māra … vanished right there.
Linked Discourses 4.5
1. Lifespan
Māra’s Snares (2nd)

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā bārāṇasiyaṁ viharati isipatane migadāye.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Varanasi in the deer park at Isipatana.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,
“Mendicants!”
“Venerable sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Muttāhaṁ, bhikkhave, sabbapāsehi ye dibbā ye ca mānusā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I am freed from all snares, both human and heavenly.

segs.p: Tumhepi, bhikkhave, muttā sabbapāsehi ye dibbā ye ca mānusā.
segs.e: You are also freed from all snares, both human and heavenly.

segs.p: Caratha, bhikkhave, cārikaṁ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.
segs.e: Wander forth, mendicants, for the welfare and happiness of the people, out of sympathy for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.
Let not two go by one road.

segs.p: Desetha, bhikkhave, dhammaṁ ādikalyāṇaṁ majjhekalyāṇaṁ pariyosānakalyāṇaṁ sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pakāsetha.
segs.e: Teach the Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And reveal a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

segs.p: Santi sattā apparajakkhajātikā, assavanatā dhammassa parihāyanti.
segs.e: There are beings with little dust in their eyes. They’re in decline because they haven’t heard the teaching.
There will be those who understand the teaching!

segs.p: Ahampi, bhikkhave, yena uruvelā senānigamo tenupasaṅkamissāmi dhammadesanāyā”ti.
segs.e: I will travel to the town of Senā in Uruvelā in order to teach the Dhamma.”

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then Māra the Wicked went up to the Buddha and addressed him in verse:
“You’re bound by all snares,
both human and heavenly.
You’re bound by the great bond:
you won’t escape me, ascetic!”
“I’m freed from all snares,
both human and heavenly.
I’m freed from the great bonds;
You’re beaten, terminator!”
Then Māra … vanished right there.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā rattandhakāratimisāyaṁ abbhokāse nisinno hoti, devo ca ekamekaṁ phusāyati.
segs.e: Now at that time the Buddha was meditating in the open during the dark of night, while a gentle rain drizzled down.

segs.e: Then Māra the Wicked, wanting to make the Buddha feel fear, terror, and goosebumps, manifested in the form of a big cobra king and approached him.
Its body was like a big canoe carved from a single tree.
Its hood was like a large brewer’s sieve.
Its eyes were like big bronze cups from Kosala.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi nāma deve gaḷagaḷāyante vijjullatā niccharanti;
segs.e: Its tongue flickered from its mouth like lightning flashes in a thunderstorm.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi nāma kammāragaggariyā dhamamānāya saddo hoti;
segs.e: The sound of its breathing was like the puffing of a blacksmith’s bellows.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā “māro ayaṁ pāpimā” iti viditvā māraṁ pāpimantaṁ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha, knowing that this was Māra the Wicked, replied to him in verse:
“One who frequents empty buildings
for lodging—that sage is self-restrained.
It’s appropriate for that sort
to live there after relinquishing.
Though there are lots of creepy crawlies,
and lots of flies and reptiles,
they wouldn’t stir a hair
of a great sage in that empty hut.
Though the firmament may split <j>and the earth may quake,
and all creatures be stricken with fear;
and even if an arrow’s aimed at their breast,
the Buddhas take no shelter in attachments.”

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṁ bhagavā, jānāti maṁ sugato”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.
segs.e: Then Māra the Wicked, thinking, “The Buddha knows me! The Holy One knows me!” miserable and sad, vanished right there.

Sleeping

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā bahudevarattiṁ abbhokāse caṅkamitvā rattiyā paccūsasamayaṁ pāde pakkhāletvā vihāraṁ pavisitvā
segs.e: He spent much of the night walking mindfully in the open. At the crack of dawn he washed his feet and entered his dwelling.

segs.p: dakkhiṇena passena sīhaseyyaṁ kappesi pāde pādaṁ accādhāya sato sampajāno uṭṭhānasaññaṁ manasi karitvā.
segs.e: He laid down in the lion’s posture—on the right side, placing one foot on top of the other—mindful and aware, and focused on the time of getting up.

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then Māra the Wicked went up to the Buddha and addressed him in verse:
“What, you’re asleep? <j>Really, you’re asleep?
You sleep like a loser—<j>what’s up with that?
You sleep, thinking that the hut is empty.
You sleep when the sun has come up—<j>what’s up with that?”
“For them there is no craving—
the weaver, the clinger—<j>to track them anywhere.
With the ending of all attachments <j>the awakened Buddha sleeps.
What’s that got to do with you, Māra?”
Then Māra … vanished right there.

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
segs.e: Then Māra the Wicked went up to the Buddha and spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:
“Children bring you delight!
Cattle also bring you delight!
For attachments are a man’s delight;

segs.p: Na hi so nandati yo nirūpadhī”ti.
segs.e: without attachments there’s no delight.”
“Your children bring you sorrow.
Your cattle also bring you sorrow.
For attachments are a man’s sorrow;

segs.p: Na hi so socati yo nirūpadhī”ti.
segs.e: without attachments there are no sorrows.”

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṁ bhagavā, jānāti maṁ sugato”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,
“Mendicants!”
“Venerable sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“Mendicants, the lifespan of humans is short.

segs.p: Gamanīyo samparāyo, kattabbaṁ kusalaṁ, caritabbaṁ brahmacariyaṁ.
segs.e: We are headed for lives to come. So we must do what is skillful, we must practice the spiritual life.
No one born is immortal.

segs.p: Yo, bhikkhave, ciraṁ jīvati, so vassasataṁ appaṁ vā bhiyyo”ti.
segs.e: A long life is a hundred years or a little more.”

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then Māra the Wicked went up to the Buddha and addressed him in verse:
“The life of humans is long!
A true person wouldn’t scorn it.
Live like a suckling babe,
for Death has not come for you.”
“The life of humans is short,
and a true person scorns it.
They should live as though their head was on fire,
for Death comes for everyone.”
Then Māra … vanished right there.

segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, on the Vulture’s Peak Mountain.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā rattandhakāratimisāyaṁ abbhokāse nisinno hoti, devo ca ekamekaṁ phusāyati.
segs.e: Now at that time the Buddha was meditating in the open during the dark of night, while a gentle rain drizzled down.

segs.e: Then Māra the Wicked, wanting to make the Buddha feel fear, terror, and goosebumps, approached him, and crushed some large boulders close by him.

segs.e: Then the Buddha, knowing that this was Māra the Wicked, addressed him in verse:

this entire Vulture’s Peak,
the rightly released,
the awakened, are unshaken.”

Lion

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā mahatiyā parisāya parivuto dhammaṁ deseti.
segs.e: Now, at that time the Buddha was teaching Dhamma, surrounded by a large assembly.
Then Māra thought,

segs.p: “ayaṁ kho samaṇo gotamo mahatiyā parisāya parivuto dhammaṁ deseti.
segs.e: “The ascetic Gotama is teaching Dhamma, surrounded by a large assembly.

segs.p: Yannūnāhaṁ yena samaṇo gotamo tenupasaṅkameyyaṁ vicakkhukammāyā”ti.
segs.e: Why don’t I go and pull the wool over their eyes?”

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then Māra the Wicked went up to the Buddha and addressed him in verse:
“Why now do you roar like a lion?
You’re so self-assured in the assembly!
For there is someone who’ll wrestle with you,
so why do you imagine you’re the victor?”
“The great heroes they roar,
self-assured in the assemblies.
The Realized One, attained to power,
has crossed over clinging to the world.”

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṁ bhagavā, jānāti maṁ sugato”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.
segs.e: Then Māra the Wicked, thinking, “The Buddha knows me! The Holy One knows me!” miserable and sad, vanished right there.

2. Rule
A Splinter
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati maddakucchismiṁ migadāye.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Maddakucchi deer park.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavato pādo sakalikāya khato hoti,
segs.e: Now at that time the Buddha’s foot had been cut by a wooden splinter.

segs.p: bhusā sudaṁ bhagavato vedanā vattanti sārīrikā dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā asātā amanāpā.
segs.e: The Buddha was stricken by harrowing pains; physical feelings that were painful, sharp, severe, acute, unpleasant, and disagreeable.

segs.p: Tā sudaṁ bhagavā sato sampajāno adhivāseti avihaññamāno.
segs.e: But he endured unbothered, with mindfulness and situational awareness.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā catugguṇaṁ saṅghāṭiṁ paññapetvā dakkhiṇena passena sīhaseyyaṁ kappesi pāde pādaṁ accādhāya sato sampajāno.
segs.e: And then he spread out his outer robe folded in four and laid down in the lion’s posture—on the right side, placing one foot on top of the other—mindful and aware.

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then Māra the Wicked went up to the Buddha and addressed him in verse:
“Are you feeble that you lie down? <j>Or are you drunk on poetry?

segs.p: Atthā nu te sampacurā na santi;
segs.e: Are your goals not amply satisfied?
Alone in a secluded lodging,
why this sleeping, sleepyhead?”
“I’m not feeble that I lie down, <j>nor am I drunk on poetry.
Having reached the goal, I’m rid of sorrow.
Alone in a secluded lodging,
I lie down full of sympathy for all living creatures.
Even those with a dart stuck in the breast,
piercing the heart moment by moment,
are able to get some sleep.
So why not I, whose dart is drawn out?

segs.p: Jaggaṁ na saṅke napi bhemi sottuṁ,
segs.e: I don’t lie awake tense, nor do I fear to sleep.
The days and nights don’t disturb me,
as I see no decline for myself in the world.
That’s why I lie down full of sympathy for all living creatures.”

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṁ bhagavā, jānāti maṁ sugato”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.
segs.e: Then Māra the Wicked, thinking, “The Buddha knows me! The Holy One knows me!” miserable and sad, vanished right there.

2. Rule
Appropriate

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kosalesu viharati ekasālāyaṁ brāhmaṇagāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Kosalans near the brahmin village of Ekasālā.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā mahatiyā gihiparisāya parivuto dhammaṁ deseti.
segs.e: Now, at that time the Buddha was teaching Dhamma, surrounded by a large assembly of laypeople.
Then Māra thought,

segs.p: “ayaṁ kho samaṇo gotamo mahatiyā gihiparisāya parivuto dhammaṁ deseti.
segs.e: “The ascetic Gotama is teaching Dhamma, surrounded by a large assembly of laypeople.

segs.p: Yannūnāhaṁ yena samaṇo gotamo tenupasaṅkameyyaṁ vicakkhukammāyā”ti.
segs.e: Why don’t I go and pull the wool over their eyes?”

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then Māra the Wicked went up to the Buddha and addressed him in verse:
“It’s not appropriate for you
to instruct others.
As you engage in this,
don’t get caught up in favoring and opposing.”
“The Buddha instructs others
out of compassion for their welfare.
The Realized One is liberated
from favoring and opposing.”

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṁ bhagavā, jānāti maṁ sugato”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.
segs.e: Then Māra the Wicked, thinking, “The Buddha knows me! The Holy One knows me!” miserable and sad, vanished right there.

2. Rule
A Mental Snare
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then Māra the Wicked went up to the Buddha and addressed him in verse:
“There’s a mental snare
wandering in midair.
I’ll bind you with it—
you won’t escape me, ascetic!”
“Sights, sounds, tastes, smells,
and touches so delightful:
desire for these is gone from me.
You’re beaten, terminator!”

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṁ bhagavā, jānāti maṁ sugato”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.
segs.e: Then Māra the Wicked, thinking, “The Buddha knows me! The Holy One knows me!” miserable and sad, vanished right there.

2. Rule
The Alms Bowls
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā pañcannaṁ upādānakkhandhānaṁ upādāya bhikkhūnaṁ dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṁseti.
segs.e: Now at that time the Buddha was educating, encouraging, firing up, and inspiring the mendicants with a Dhamma talk on the topic of the five grasping aggregates.

segs.p: Te ca bhikkhū aṭṭhiṁ katvā manasi katvā sabbacetasā samannāharitvā ohitasotā dhammaṁ suṇanti.
segs.e: And those mendicants were paying attention, applying the mind, concentrating wholeheartedly, and actively listening.
Then Māra thought,

segs.p: “ayaṁ kho samaṇo gotamo pañcannaṁ upādānakkhandhānaṁ upādāya bhikkhūnaṁ dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṁseti.
segs.e: “This ascetic Gotama is educating, encouraging, firing up, and inspiring the mendicants with a Dhamma talk on the topic of the five grasping aggregates.

segs.p: Te ca bhikkhū aṭṭhiṁ katvā manasi katvā sabbacetasā samannāharitvā ohitasotā dhammaṁ suṇanti.
segs.e: And the mendicants are paying attention, applying the mind, concentrating wholeheartedly, and actively listening.

segs.p: Yannūnāhaṁ yena samaṇo gotamo tenupasaṅkameyyaṁ vicakkhukammāyā”ti.
segs.e: Why don’t I go and pull the wool over their eyes?”

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā pattā abbhokāse nikkhittā honti.
segs.e: At that time several alms bowls were placed in the open air.

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā balībaddavaṇṇaṁ abhinimminitvā yena te pattā tenupasaṅkami.
segs.e: Then Māra the Wicked manifested in the form of an ox and approached those bowls.

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu aññataraṁ bhikkhuṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: One of the mendicants said to another,
“Mendicant, mendicant, that ox will break the bowls.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, bhagavā taṁ bhikkhuṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When this was said, the Buddha said to that mendicant,
“Mendicant, that’s no ox.

segs.p: Māro eso pāpimā tumhākaṁ vicakkhukammāya āgato”ti.
segs.e: That’s Māra the Wicked come to pull the wool over your eyes!”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā “māro ayaṁ pāpimā” iti viditvā māraṁ pāpimantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha, knowing that this was Māra the Wicked, addressed him in verse:
“Form, what is felt, and perception,
consciousness, and what is chosen:
‘I am not this’ and ‘this is not mine’;
that’s how they become free of desire for them.
When you’re detached, secure,
all fetters transcended,
though Māra and his army chase everywhere
they never find you.”
Then Māra … vanished right there.

2. Rule
The Six Fields of Contact

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā vesāliyaṁ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṁ.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā channaṁ phassāyatanānaṁ upādāya bhikkhūnaṁ dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṁseti.
segs.e: Now at that time the Buddha was educating, encouraging, firing up, and inspiring the mendicants with a Dhamma talk on the topic of the six fields of contact.

segs.p: Te ca bhikkhū aṭṭhiṁ katvā manasi katvā sabbacetasā samannāharitvā ohitasotā dhammaṁ suṇanti.
segs.e: And those mendicants were paying attention, applying the mind, concentrating wholeheartedly, and actively listening.
Then Māra thought,

segs.p: “ayaṁ kho samaṇo gotamo channaṁ phassāyatanānaṁ upādāya bhikkhūnaṁ dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sappahaṁseti.
segs.e: “This ascetic Gotama is educating, encouraging, firing up, and inspiring the mendicants with a Dhamma talk on the topic of the six fields of contact.

segs.p: Te ca bhikkhū aṭṭhiṁ katvā manasi katvā sabbacetasā samannāharitvā ohitasotā dhammaṁ suṇanti.
segs.e: And those mendicants are paying attention, applying the mind, concentrating wholeheartedly, and actively listening.

segs.p: Yannūnāhaṁ yena samaṇo gotamo tenupasaṅkameyyaṁ vicakkhukammāyā”ti.
segs.e: Why don’t I go and pull the wool over their eyes?”

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato avidūre mahantaṁ bhayabheravaṁ saddamakāsi, apissudaṁ pathavī maññe undrīyati. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu aññataraṁ bhikkhuṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Māra the Wicked went up to the Buddha and made a terrifyingly loud noise close by him. It seemed as if the earth were shattering, so that one of the mendicants said to another,
“Mendicant, mendicant, it seems like the earth is shattering!”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, bhagavā taṁ bhikkhuṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When this was said, the Buddha said to that mendicant,
“Mendicant, that’s not the earth shattering.

segs.p: Māro eso pāpimā tumhākaṁ vicakkhukammāya āgato”ti.
segs.e: That’s Māra the Wicked come to pull the wool over your eyes!”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā “māro ayaṁ pāpimā” iti viditvā māraṁ pāpimantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha, knowing that this was Māra the Wicked, addressed him in verse:
“Sights, sounds, tastes, smells,
touches, and ideas, the lot of them—
this is the terrible bait
that the world’s infatuated by.
But a mindful disciple of the Buddha
has transcended all that.
Having slipped free of Māra’s dominion,
they dazzle like the sun.”
Then Māra … vanished right there.

2. Rule
Alms Food

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā magadhesu viharati pañcasālāyaṁ brāhmaṇagāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Magadhans near the brahmin village of Pañcasālā.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena pañcasālāyaṁ brāhmaṇagāme kumārikānaṁ pāhunakāni bhavanti.
segs.e: Now at that time in Pañcasālā the young maidens were occupied with guests.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya pañcasālaṁ brāhmaṇagāmaṁ piṇḍāya pāvisi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Pañcasālā for alms.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena pañcasāleyyakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā mārena pāpimatā anvāviṭṭhā bhavanti:
segs.e: Now at that time Māra had possessed the brahmins and householders of Pañcasālā, so that they thought,
“Don’t let the ascetic Gotama get any alms!”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā yathādhotena pattena pañcasālaṁ brāhmaṇagāmaṁ piṇḍāya pāvisi tathādhotena pattena paṭikkami.
segs.e: Then the Buddha left the village with his bowl as clean-washed as it was when he entered for alms.

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Māra the Wicked went up to the Buddha and said to him,
“Well, ascetic, did you get any alms?”

segs.p: “Tathā nu tvaṁ, pāpima, akāsi yathāhaṁ piṇḍaṁ na labheyyan”ti.
segs.e: “Wicked One, did you make sure I didn’t get any alms?”

segs.p: “Tena hi, bhante, bhagavā dutiyampi pañcasālaṁ brāhmaṇagāmaṁ piṇḍāya pavisatu.
segs.e: “Well then, sir, let the Buddha enter Pañcasālā a second time for alms.

segs.p: Tathāhaṁ karissāmi yathā bhagavā piṇḍaṁ lacchatī”ti.
segs.e: I’ll make sure you get alms.”
“Māra has produced wickedness
in attacking the Realized One.
Wicked One, do you imagine that
your wickedness won’t bear fruit?
Let us live so very happily,
we who have nothing.
We shall feed on rapture,
like the gods of sublime luminosity.”

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṁ bhagavā, jānāti maṁ sugato”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.
segs.e: Then Māra the Wicked, thinking, “The Buddha knows me! The Holy One knows me!” miserable and sad, vanished right there.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā bhikkhūnaṁ nibbānapaṭisaṁyuttāya dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṁseti.
segs.e: Now at that time the Buddha was educating, encouraging, firing up, and inspiring the mendicants with a Dhamma talk about extinguishment.

segs.e: Then Māra the Wicked manifested in the form of a farmer carrying a large plough on his shoulder. He held a long goad, his hair was messy, he was clad in sunn hemp, and his feet were muddy. He went up to the Buddha and said to him,
“So, ascetic, did you happen to see any oxen?”
“But what have you to do with oxen, Wicked One?”

segs.p: “Mameva, samaṇa, cakkhu, mama rūpā, mama cakkhusamphassaviññāṇāyatanaṁ.
segs.e: “Mine alone, ascetic, is the eye, mine are sights, mine is the field of eye contact consciousness.
Where can you escape me, ascetic?
Mine alone is the ear …
nose …
tongue …
body …

segs.p: mameva, samaṇa, mano, mama dhammā, mama manosamphassaviññāṇāyatanaṁ.
segs.e: mind, mine are ideas, mine is the field of mind contact consciousness.

Taveva, pāpima, ghānaṁ, tava gandhā, tava ghānasamphassaviññāṇāyatanaṁ.
segs.e: nose …

“The things they call ‘mine’,
and those who say ‘it’s mine’:
if your mind remains there,
you won’t escape me, ascetic!”
“The things they speak of aren’t mine;
I’m not someone who speaks like that.
So know this, Wicked One:
you won’t even see the path I take.”
Then Māra … vanished right there.

2. Rule
Ruling

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kosalesu viharati himavantapadese araññakuṭikāyaṁ.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Kosalans, in a wilderness hut on the slopes of the Himalayas.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavato rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṁ cetaso parivitakko udapādi:
segs.e: Then as he was in private retreat this thought came to his mind,

segs.p: “sakkā nu kho rajjaṁ kāretuṁ ahanaṁ aghātayaṁ ajinaṁ ajāpayaṁ asocaṁ asocāpayaṁ dhammenā”ti?
segs.e: “I wonder if it’s possible to rule legitimately, without killing or having someone kill for you; without conquering or having someone conquer for you; without sorrowing or causing sorrow?”

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā bhagavato cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: And then Māra the Wicked, knowing the Buddha’s train of thought, went up to him and said,

segs.p: “kāretu, bhante, bhagavā rajjaṁ, kāretu, sugato, rajjaṁ ahanaṁ aghātayaṁ ajinaṁ ajāpayaṁ asocaṁ asocāpayaṁ dhammenā”ti.
segs.e: “Rule, Blessed One! Rule, Holy One! Rule legitimately, without killing or having someone kill for you; without conquering or having someone conquer for you; without sorrowing or causing sorrow!”

segs.p: “Kiṁ pana me tvaṁ, pāpima, passasi yaṁ maṁ tvaṁ evaṁ vadesi:
segs.e: “But what do you see, Wicked One, that you say this to me?”

segs.p: ‘kāretu, bhante, bhagavā rajjaṁ, kāretu sugato, rajjaṁ ahanaṁ aghātayaṁ ajinaṁ ajāpayaṁ asocaṁ asocāpayaṁ dhammenā’”ti?
“Bhagavatā kho, bhante, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā.
segs.e: “The Blessed One, sir, has developed and cultivated the four bases for psychic power, made them a vehicle and a basis, kept them up, consolidated them, and properly implemented them.

segs.p: Ākaṅkhamāno ca, bhante, bhagavā himavantaṁ pabbatarājaṁ suvaṇṇaṁ tveva adhimucceyya suvaṇṇañca panassā”ti.
segs.e: If he wished, the Blessed One need only determine that the Himalaya, king of mountains, was gold, and it would turn into gold.”
“Take a golden mountain,
entirely of native gold, and double it—
it’s still not enough for one!
Knowing this, live a moral life.
When a personage has seen where suffering comes from
how could they incline toward sensual pleasures?
Realizing that attachment is a chain in the world,
a personage would train to remove it.”

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṁ bhagavā, jānāti maṁ sugato”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.
segs.e: Then Māra the Wicked, thinking, “The Buddha knows me! The Holy One knows me!” miserable and sad, vanished right there.

3. Māra
Several
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sakkesu viharati silāvatiyaṁ.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Sakyans near Silāvatī.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū bhagavato avidūre appamattā ātāpino pahitattā viharanti.
segs.e: Now at that time several mendicants were meditating not far from the Buddha, diligent, keen, and resolute.

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā brāhmaṇavaṇṇaṁ abhinimminitvā mahantena jaṭaṇḍuvena ajinakkhipanivattho jiṇṇo gopānasivaṅko ghurughurupassāsī udumbaradaṇḍaṁ gahetvā yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te bhikkhū etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Māra the Wicked manifested in the form of a brahmin with a large matted dreadlock, wearing an antelope hide. He was old, bent double, wheezing, and held a staff made of cluster fig tree wood. He went up to those mendicants and said,

segs.p: “daharā bhavanto pabbajitā susū kāḷakesā bhadrena yobbanena samannāgatā paṭhamena vayasā anikkīḷitāvino kāmesu.
segs.e: “You’ve gone forth while young, reverends.  With pristine black hair, you’re blessed with youth, in the prime of life, and you’ve never flirted with sensual pleasures.
Enjoy human sensual pleasures.
Don’t give up what is apparent in the present to chase after what takes effect over time.”

segs.p: “Na kho mayaṁ, brāhmaṇa, sandiṭṭhikaṁ hitvā kālikaṁ anudhāvāma.
segs.e: “Brahmin, that’s not what we’re doing.

segs.p: Kālikañca kho mayaṁ, brāhmaṇa, hitvā sandiṭṭhikaṁ anudhāvāma.
segs.e: We’re giving up what takes effect over time to chase after what is apparent in the present.

segs.p: Kālikā hi, brāhmaṇa, kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo.
segs.e: For the Buddha says that sensual pleasures take effect over time; they give much suffering and distress, and they are all the more full of drawbacks.

segs.p: Sandiṭṭhiko ayaṁ dhammo akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhī”ti.
segs.e: But this teaching is apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, māro pāpimā sīsaṁ okampetvā jivhaṁ nillāletvā tivisākhaṁ nalāṭe nalāṭikaṁ vuṭṭhāpetvā daṇḍamolubbha pakkāmi.
segs.e: When they had spoken, Māra the Wicked shook his head, waggled his tongue, raised his eyebrows until his brow puckered in three furrows, and left leaning on his staff.

segs.p: Atha kho te bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then those mendicants went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened. The Buddha said,

segs.p: “idha mayaṁ, bhante, bhagavato avidūre appamattā ātāpino pahitattā viharāma.
Atha kho, bhante, aññataro brāhmaṇo mahantena jaṭaṇḍuvena ajinakkhipanivattho jiṇṇo gopānasivaṅko ghurughurupassāsī udumbaradaṇḍaṁ gahetvā yena mayaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā amhe etadavoca:
‘daharā bhavanto pabbajitā susū kāḷakesā bhadrena yobbanena samannāgatā paṭhamena vayasā anikkīḷitāvino kāmesu.
Evaṁ vutte, mayaṁ, bhante, taṁ brāhmaṇaṁ etadavocumha:
‘na kho mayaṁ, brāhmaṇa, sandiṭṭhikaṁ hitvā kālikaṁ anudhāvāma.
Kālikañca kho mayaṁ, brāhmaṇa, hitvā sandiṭṭhikaṁ anudhāvāma.
Kālikā hi, brāhmaṇa, kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo.
Sandiṭṭhiko ayaṁ dhammo akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhī’ti.
Evaṁ vutte, bhante, so brāhmaṇo sīsaṁ okampetvā jivhaṁ nillāletvā tivisākhaṁ nalāṭe nalāṭikaṁ vuṭṭhāpetvā daṇḍamolubbha pakkanto”ti.

segs.e: “Mendicants, that was no brahmin.

segs.p: Māro eso pāpimā tumhākaṁ vicakkhukammāya āgato”ti.
segs.e: That was Māra the Wicked who came to pull the wool over your eyes!”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
segs.e: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha spoke this verse:
“When a personage has seen where suffering comes from
how could they incline toward sensual pleasures?
Realizing that attachment is a chain in the world,
a personage would train to remove it.”
Linked Discourses 4.22
3. Māra
With Samiddhi

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sakkesu viharati silāvatiyaṁ.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Sakyans near Silāvatī.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā samiddhi bhagavato avidūre appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharati.
segs.e: Now at that time Venerable Samiddhi was meditating not far from the Buddha, diligent, keen, and resolute.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmato samiddhissa rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṁ cetaso parivitakko udapādi:
segs.e: Then as Venerable Samiddhi was in private retreat this thought came to his mind,
“I’m so fortunate, so very fortunate,
to have a teacher who is a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha!

segs.p: Lābhā vata me, suladdhaṁ vata me,
segs.e: I’m so fortunate, so very fortunate,
to have gone forth in a teaching and training so well explained!

segs.p: Lābhā vata me, suladdhaṁ vata me,
segs.e: I’m so fortunate, so very fortunate,
to have spiritual companions who are ethical and of good character.”

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā āyasmato samiddhissa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya yenāyasmā samiddhi tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmato samiddhissa avidūre mahantaṁ bhayabheravaṁ saddamakāsi, apissudaṁ pathavī maññe undrīyati.
segs.e: And then Māra the Wicked, knowing Samiddhi’s train of thought, went up to him and made a terrifyingly loud noise close by him. It seemed as if the earth was shattering.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā samiddhi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno āyasmā samiddhi bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Samiddhi went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened. The Buddha said,

segs.p: “idhāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavato avidūre appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharāmi.
Tassa mayhaṁ, bhante, rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṁ cetaso parivitakko udapādi:
Lābhā vata me, suladdhaṁ vata me,
Lābhā vata me, suladdhaṁ vata me,
Tassa mayhaṁ, bhante, avidūre mahābhayabheravasaddo ahosi, apissudaṁ pathavī maññe undrīyatī”ti.

segs.e: “Samiddhi, that’s not the earth shattering.

segs.p: Māro eso pāpimā tuyhaṁ vicakkhukammāya āgato.
segs.e: That’s Māra the Wicked come to pull the wool over your eyes!

segs.p: Gaccha tvaṁ, samiddhi, tattheva appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharāhī”ti.
segs.e: Go back to that same place, Samiddhi, and meditate, diligent, keen, and resolute.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā samiddhi bhagavato paṭissutvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā pakkāmi.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” replied Samiddhi. He rose from his seat, bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before leaving.

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho āyasmā samiddhi tattheva appamatto ātāpī pahitatto vihāsi.
segs.e: And for a second time Samiddhi was meditating in that same place, diligent, ardent, and resolute.

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho āyasmato samiddhissa rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa …pe…
segs.e: And for a second time he had the same thought …

segs.p: dutiyampi kho māro pāpimā āyasmato samiddhissa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya …pe…
segs.e: and Māra made an earth-shattering noise.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā samiddhi māraṁ pāpimantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then Samiddhi addressed Māra the Wicked in verse:
“I went forth out of faith
from the lay life to homelessness.
My mindfulness and wisdom are mature,
my mind is serene in immersion.
Make whatever illusions you want,
it won’t bother me.”

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṁ samiddhi bhikkhū”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.
segs.e: Then Māra the Wicked, thinking, “The mendicant Samiddhi knows me!” miserable and sad, vanished right there.
Linked Discourses 4.23
3. Māra
With Godhika
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā godhiko isigilipasse viharati kāḷasilāyaṁ.
segs.e: Now at that time Venerable Godhika was staying on the slopes of Isigili at the Black Rock.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā godhiko appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto sāmayikaṁ cetovimuttiṁ phusi.
segs.e: Then Venerable Godhika, meditating diligent, keen, and resolute, experienced temporary freedom of heart.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā godhiko tamhā sāmayikāya cetovimuttiyā parihāyi.
segs.e: But then he fell away from that temporary freedom of heart.

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho āyasmā godhiko appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto sāmayikaṁ cetovimuttiṁ phusi.
segs.e: For a second …

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho āyasmā godhiko tamhā sāmayikāya cetovimuttiyā parihāyi.
Tatiyampi kho āyasmā godhiko appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto sāmayikaṁ cetovimuttiṁ phusi.
segs.e: third …

segs.p: Tatiyampi kho āyasmā godhiko tamhā …pe… parihāyi.
Catutthampi kho āyasmā godhiko appamatto …pe… vimuttiṁ phusi.
segs.e: fourth …

segs.p: Catutthampi kho āyasmā godhiko tamhā …pe… parihāyi.
Pañcamampi kho āyasmā godhiko …pe… cetovimuttiṁ phusi.
segs.e: fifth …

segs.p: Chaṭṭhampi kho āyasmā godhiko appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto sāmayikaṁ cetovimuttiṁ phusi.
segs.e: sixth time Godhika experienced temporary freedom of heart.

segs.p: Chaṭṭhampi kho āyasmā godhiko tamhā sāmayikāya cetovimuttiyā parihāyi.
segs.e: But for a sixth time he fell away from it.

segs.p: Sattamampi kho āyasmā godhiko appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto sāmayikaṁ cetovimuttiṁ phusi.
segs.e: For a seventh time Godhika, meditating diligent, keen, and resolute, experienced temporary freedom of heart.
Then he thought,
“I’ve fallen away from this temporary freedom of heart no less than six times.
Why don’t I commit suicide?”

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā āyasmato godhikassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: And then Māra the Wicked, knowing Godhika’s train of thought, went up to the Buddha and addressed him in verse:
“O great hero, O greatly wise!
Shining with power and glory.
You’ve gone beyond all enmities and fears,
I bow to your feet, O Clear-eyed One!
Great hero, master of death,
your disciple longs for death,
he’s planning for it.
Stop him, O light-bringer!
For Blessed One, renowned among men,
your disciple who loves your teaching,
a trainee who hasn’t achieved their heart’s desire—
how can they kill themselves?”

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmatā godhikena satthaṁ āharitaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Now at that time Venerable Godhika had already committed suicide.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā “māro ayaṁ pāpimā” iti viditvā māraṁ pāpimantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha, knowing that this was Māra the Wicked, addressed him in verse:
“This is how the attentive act,
for they don’t long for life.
Having plucked out craving, root and all,
Godhika is quenched.”
Then the Buddha said to the mendicants,

segs.p: “āyāma, bhikkhave, yena isigilipassaṁ kāḷasilā tenupasaṅkamissāma yattha godhikena kulaputtena satthaṁ āharitan”ti.
segs.e: “Come, mendicants, let’s go to the Black Rock on the slopes of Isigili where Godhika, who came from a good family, committed suicide.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā sambahulehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṁ yena isigilipassaṁ kāḷasilā tenupasaṅkami.
segs.e: Then the Buddha together with several mendicants went to the Black Rock on the slopes of Isigili.

segs.p: Addasā kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ godhikaṁ dūratova mañcake vivattakkhandhaṁ semānaṁ.
segs.e: The Buddha saw Godhika off in the distance on his cot, lying with aggregates cast off.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena dhūmāyitattaṁ timirāyitattaṁ gacchateva purimaṁ disaṁ, gacchati pacchimaṁ disaṁ, gacchati uttaraṁ disaṁ, gacchati dakkhiṇaṁ disaṁ, gacchati uddhaṁ, gacchati adho, gacchati anudisaṁ.
segs.e: Now at that time a cloud of black smoke was moving east, west, north, south, above, below, and in-between.
Then the Buddha said to the mendicants,

segs.p: “passatha no tumhe, bhikkhave, etaṁ dhūmāyitattaṁ timirāyitattaṁ gacchateva purimaṁ disaṁ, gacchati pacchimaṁ disaṁ, gacchati uttaraṁ disaṁ, gacchati dakkhiṇaṁ disaṁ, gacchati uddhaṁ, gacchati adho, gacchati anudisan”ti?
segs.e: “Mendicants, do you see that cloud of black smoke moving east, west, north, south, above, below, and in-between?”
“Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Eso kho, bhikkhave, māro pāpimā godhikassa kulaputtassa viññāṇaṁ samanvesati:
segs.e: “That’s Māra the Wicked searching for Godhika’s consciousness, wondering:
‘Where is Godhika’s consciousness established?’

segs.p: Appatiṭṭhitena ca, bhikkhave, viññāṇena godhiko kulaputto parinibbuto”ti.
segs.e: But since his consciousness is not established, Godhika is quenched.”

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā beluvapaṇḍuvīṇaṁ ādāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then Māra, carrying his arched harp made from the pale timber of wood-apple, went up to the Buddha and addressed him in verse:
“Above, below, all round,
in the four quarters and in-between,
I’ve been searching without success:
where has that Godhika got to?”
“He was an attentive and steadfast sage,
a meditator who loved absorption.
By day and by night he applied himself,
without concern for his life.
He defeated the army of death,
and won’t return for any future life.
Having plucked out craving, root and all
Godhika is quenched.”
So stricken with sorrow
that his harp dropped from his armpit,
that spirit, downcast,
vanished right there.
Linked Discourses 4.24
3. Māra
Seven Years of Pursuit
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā uruvelāyaṁ viharati najjā nerañjarāya tīre ajapālanigrodhe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in Uruvelā at the goatherd’s banyan tree on the bank of the Nerañjarā River.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena māro pāpimā sattavassāni bhagavantaṁ anubandho hoti otārāpekkho otāraṁ alabhamāno.
segs.e: Now at that time Māra the Wicked had been pursuing the Buddha for seven years hoping to find a vulnerability without success.

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then Māra the Wicked went up to the Buddha and addressed him in verse:
“Are you swamped by sorrow <j>that you meditate in the forest?
Have you lost a fortune, or do you long for one?
Or perhaps you’ve committed <j>some crime in the village?
Why don’t you get too close to people?
And why does no one get close to you?”
“I’ve dug out the root of sorrow completely.
I practice absorption free of guilt or sorrow.
I’ve cut off all greed and muttered prayer for future lives.
Undefiled, I practice absorption, <j>O kinsman of the negligent!”
“The things they call ‘mine’,
and those who say ‘it’s mine’:
if your mind remains there,
you won’t escape me, ascetic!”
“The things they speak of aren’t mine;
I’m not someone who speaks like that.
So know this, Wicked One:
you won’t even see the path I take.”
“If you’ve discovered the path
that’s safe, and leads to freedom from death,
go and walk that path alone—
why teach it to anyone else?”
“Those crossing to the far shore
ask what’s beyond the domain of Death.
When I’m asked, I explain to them
the truth without attachments.”

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi, bhante, gāmassa vā nigamassa vā avidūre pokkharaṇī.
segs.e: “Sir, suppose there was a lotus pond not far from a town or village,
and a crab lived there.

segs.p: Atha kho, bhante, sambahulā kumārakā vā kumārikāyo vā tamhā gāmā vā nigamā vā nikkhamitvā yena sā pokkharaṇī tenupasaṅkameyyuṁ; upasaṅkamitvā taṁ kakkaṭakaṁ udakā uddharitvā thale patiṭṭhapeyyuṁ.
segs.e: Then several boys or girls would leave the town or village and go to the pond, where they’d pull out the crab and put it on solid ground.

segs.p: Yaṁ yadeva hi so, bhante, kakkaṭako aḷaṁ abhininnāmeyya taṁ tadeva te kumārakā vā kumārikāyo vā kaṭṭhena vā kathalāya vā sañchindeyyuṁ sambhañjeyyuṁ sampalibhañjeyyuṁ.
segs.e: Whenever that crab extended a claw, those boys or girls would snap, crack, and break it off with a stick or a stone.

segs.p: Evañhi so, bhante, kakkaṭako sabbehi aḷehi sañchinnehi sambhaggehi sampalibhaggehi abhabbo taṁ pokkharaṇiṁ otarituṁ.
segs.e: And when that crab’s claws had all been snapped, cracked, and broken off it wouldn’t be able to return down into that lotus pond.

segs.p: Evameva kho, bhante, yāni kānici visūkāyikāni visevitāni vipphanditāni, sabbāni tāni bhagavatā sañchinnāni sambhaggāni sampalibhaggāni.
segs.e: In the same way, sir, the Buddha has snapped, cracked, and broken off all my twists, ducks, and dodges.

segs.p: Abhabbo dānāhaṁ, bhante, puna bhagavantaṁ upasaṅkamituṁ yadidaṁ otārāpekkho”ti.
segs.e: Now I’m not able to approach the Buddha again in hopes of finding a vulnerability.”

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā bhagavato santike imā nibbejanīyā gāthāyo abhāsi:
segs.e: Then Māra the Wicked recited these verses of disappointment in the Buddha’s presence:
“A crow once circled a stone
that looked like a lump of fat.
‘Perhaps I’ll find something tender,’ it thought,
‘perhaps there’s something tasty.’
But finding nothing tasty,
the crow left that place.
Like the crow that pecked the stone,
I leave Gotama disappointed.”
Linked Discourses 4.25
3. Māra
Māra’s Daughters

segs.p: Atha kho māro pāpimā bhagavato santike imā nibbejanīyā gāthāyo abhāsitvā tamhā ṭhānā apakkamma bhagavato avidūre pathaviyaṁ pallaṅkena nisīdi tuṇhībhūto maṅkubhūto pattakkhandho adhomukho pajjhāyanto appaṭibhāno kaṭṭhena bhūmiṁ vilikhanto.
segs.e: And then Māra the Wicked, after reciting these verses of disillusionment in the Buddha’s presence, left that place. He sat cross-legged on the ground not far from the Buddha, silent, dismayed, shoulders drooping, downcast, depressed, with nothing to say, scratching the ground with a stick.

segs.p: Atha kho taṇhā ca arati ca ragā ca māradhītaro yena māro pāpimā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā māraṁ pāpimantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsiṁsu:
segs.e: Then Māra’s daughters Craving, Malignancy, and Lust went up to Māra the Wicked, and addressed him in verse:
“Why so downhearted, dad?
What man are you upset about?
We’ll catch him with the snare of lust,
like an elephant in the wild.
We’ll tie him up and bring him back—
he’ll fall under your sway!”
“In this world he is the perfected one, the Holy One.
He’s not easily seduced by lust.
He has slipped free of Māra’s dominion;
that’s why I’m so upset.”

segs.p: Atha kho taṇhā ca arati ca ragā ca māradhītaro yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then Māra’s daughters Craving, Malignancy, and Lust went up to the Buddha, and said to him,
“We serve at your feet, ascetic.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā na manasākāsi, yathā taṁ anuttare upadhisaṅkhaye vimutto.
segs.e: But the Buddha ignored them, since he was freed with the supreme ending of attachments.

segs.p: Atha kho taṇhā ca arati ca ragā ca māradhītaro ekamantaṁ apakkamma evaṁ samacintesuṁ:
segs.e: Then Craving, Malignancy, and Lust withdrew to one side to think up a plan.
“Men have a diverse spectrum of tastes.

segs.p: Yannūna mayaṁ ekasataṁ ekasataṁ kumārivaṇṇasataṁ abhinimmineyyāmā”ti.
segs.e: Why don’t we each manifest in the form of a hundred young maidens?”

segs.p: Atha kho taṇhā ca arati ca ragā ca māradhītaro ekasataṁ ekasataṁ kumārivaṇṇasataṁ abhinimminitvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: So that’s what they did. Then they went up to the Buddha and said to him,
“We serve at your feet, ascetic.”

segs.p: Tampi bhagavā na manasākāsi, yathā taṁ anuttare upadhisaṅkhaye vimutto.
segs.e: But the Buddha still ignored them, since he was freed with the supreme ending of attachments.

segs.p: Atha kho taṇhā ca arati ca ragā ca māradhītaro ekamantaṁ apakkamma evaṁ samacintesuṁ:
segs.e: Then Craving, Malignancy, and Lust withdrew to one side to think up a plan.
“Men have a diverse spectrum of tastes.

segs.p: Yannūna mayaṁ ekasataṁ ekasataṁ avijātavaṇṇasataṁ abhinimmineyyāmā”ti.
segs.e: Why don’t we each manifest in the form of a hundred women who have never given birth?”

segs.p: Atha kho taṇhā ca arati ca ragā ca māradhītaro ekasataṁ ekasataṁ avijātavaṇṇasataṁ abhinimminitvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: So that’s what they did. Then they went up to the Buddha and said to him,
“We serve at your feet, ascetic.”

segs.p: Tampi bhagavā na manasākāsi, yathā taṁ anuttare upadhisaṅkhaye vimutto.
segs.e: But the Buddha still ignored them, since he was freed with the supreme ending of attachments.
Then Craving, Malignancy, and Lust …

segs.p: yannūna mayaṁ ekasataṁ ekasataṁ sakiṁ vijātavaṇṇasataṁ abhinimmineyyāmāti.
sakiṁ vijātavaṇṇasataṁ abhinimminitvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: each manifested in the form of a hundred women who have given birth once …

segs.p: Tampi bhagavā na manasākāsi, yathā taṁ anuttare upadhisaṅkhaye vimutto.
yannūna mayaṁ ekasataṁ ekasataṁ duvijātavaṇṇasataṁ abhinimmineyyāmāti.

segs.e: women who have given birth twice …
middle-aged women …
old women …
But the Buddha still ignored them, since he was freed with the supreme ending of attachments.

segs.p: Atha kho taṇhā ca arati ca ragā ca māradhītaro ekamantaṁ apakkamma etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then Craving, Malignancy, and Lust withdrew to one side and said,
“What our father said is true:
‘In this world he is the perfected one, the Holy One.
He’s not easily seduced by lust.
He has slipped free of Māra’s dominion;
that’s why I’m so upset.’

segs.p: Yañhi mayaṁ samaṇaṁ vā brāhmaṇaṁ vā avītarāgaṁ iminā upakkamena upakkameyyāma hadayaṁ vāssa phaleyya, uṇhaṁ lohitaṁ vā mukhato uggaccheyya, ummādaṁ vā pāpuṇeyya cittakkhepaṁ vā.
segs.e: For if we had come on to any ascetic or brahmin like this who was not free of lust, his heart would explode, or he’d spew hot blood from his mouth, or he’d go mad or lose his mind.

segs.p: Seyyathā vā pana naḷo harito luto ussussati visussati milāyati;
segs.e: He’d dry up, wither away, and shrivel up like a green reed that was mowed down.”

segs.p: Atha kho taṇhā ca arati ca ragā ca māradhītaro yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhaṁsu.
segs.e: Then Māra’s daughters Craving, Malignancy, and Lust went up to the Buddha, and stood to one side.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho taṇhā māradhītā bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Māra’s daughter Craving addressed the Buddha in verse:
“Are you swamped by sorrow <j>that you meditate in the forest?
Have you lost a fortune, or do you long for one?
Or perhaps you’ve committed <j>some crime in the village?
Why don’t you get too close to people?
And why does no one get close to you?”
“I’ve reached the goal, peace of heart.
Having conquered the army <j>of the likable and pleasant,
alone, practicing absorption, I awakened to bliss.
That’s why I don’t get too close to people,
and no one gets too close to me.”

segs.p: Atha kho arati māradhītā bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then Māra’s daughter Malignancy addressed the Buddha in verse:
“How does a mendicant who has crossed five floods
usually meditate here while crossing the sixth?
How do they usually practice absorption <j>so that sensual perceptions
are blocked out and don’t get hold of them?”
“With tranquil body and mind well freed,
without making choices, mindful, homeless;
understanding the teaching, <j>they practice absorption without placing the mind;

segs.p: Na kuppati na sarati na thino.
segs.e: they’re not shaking or drifting or rigid.
That’s how a mendicant who has crossed five floods
usually meditates here while crossing the sixth.
That’s how they usually practice absorption <j>so that sensual perceptions
are blocked out and don’t get hold of them.”

segs.p: Atha kho ragā māradhītā bhagavato santike gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then Māra’s daughter Lust addressed the Buddha in verse:
“He lives with his community after cutting off craving,
and many of the faithful will cross over for sure.
Alas, this homeless one will snatch many men away,
and lead them past the King of Death!”
“The great heroes they lead
by means of the true teaching.
When the Realized Ones are leading by the teaching,
how could anyone who knows be jealous?”

segs.p: Atha kho taṇhā ca arati ca ragā ca māradhītaro yena māro pāpimā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu.
segs.e: Then Māra’s daughters Craving, Malignancy, and Lust went up to Māra the Wicked.

segs.p: Addasā kho māro pāpimā taṇhañca aratiñca ragañca māradhītaro dūratova āgacchantiyo.
segs.e: Māra the Wicked saw them coming off in the distance,
and addressed them in verse:
“Fools! You drill into a mountain
with lotus stalks!
You dig up a hill with your nails!
You chew iron with your teeth!
You seek a footing in the abyss, as it were,
while lifting a rock with your head!
After attacking a stump with your breast, as it were,
you leave Gotama disappointed.”
They came dazzling—
Craving, Malignancy, and Lust.
But the Teacher brushed them off right there,
like the gale, a fallen tuft.
The Linked Discourses with Māra are complete.
